test_title: PYST 2: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Transform the following sentence into active voice.

The dishes have been prepared with great care and perfection by the cook.

options.text: The cook have prepared the dishes with great care and perfection.
The cook has prepared the dishes with great care and perfection.
The cook has prepared the dishes by great care and perfection.
The cook has prepared the dish with great care and perfection.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The subject (the doer) performs the action, followed by the verb and the object.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The dishes have been prepared with great care and perfection by the cook."
 
• The sentence is in the **Present Perfect** tense. The passive form is *has/have + been + V3 (Past Participle)*. To convert it to active voice, the structure is: *Subject + has/have + V3 + Object*.
 
• To convert to active voice: Identify the agent "the cook" and place it at the beginning as the subject.
 
• Since "the cook" is a **singular subject**, the auxiliary verb must be "has" to ensure subject-verb agreement.
 
• Change the passive verb "have been prepared" to the active form "has prepared."
 
• Place the original subject "the dishes" after the verb as the object.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The cook has prepared the dishes with great care and perfection."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The cook have prepared..." – Incorrect because "have" does not agree with the singular subject "the cook."
 
• **Option 3: **"The cook has prepared the dishes by great care..." – Incorrect because the preposition "by" is used incorrectly; the original sentence uses "with" to indicate the manner of preparation.
 
• **Option 4: **"The cook has prepared the dish..." – Incorrect because it changes the plural "dishes" to the singular "dish."
